title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit:  Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Saturdays
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? You’ve mastered the basics, now it’s time to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

**What You’ll Learn**

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

**• The Cross Body Lead (CBL) Series:** Master both **Inside and Outside Turns**, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

**• The “I Turn – You Turn”:** A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

**• The Walk-Through:** Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

**• Footwork & Shine:** We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

**Technique & Artistry**

Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

**• The Frame:** Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

**• Upper Body Mechanics:** Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

**• Connection:** Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

**Important Details**

**• No dance experience required:** Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

**• No partner necessary:** Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

**•** Please wear **non-marking shoe soles:** This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

**Saturday 11:00 AM**

Instructor: Lucie Ebnerova

Address: 4140 Redwood Highway #8 San Rafael, CA

Note: Arrive 10 minutes before. No floor marking shoe soles allowed.

title: The Mayflower: An Interesting Mix of Passengers
description:
The Sonoma County Genealogical Society Presents

 **The Mayflower: An Interesting Mix of Passengers**

 **Presented by Suzanne Brayer**

 In 1620, an English merchant ship, The Mayflower, left Southampton England for the New World carrying 102 men, women, children and a crew of 30. What motivated them to embark on this incredibly dangerous journey into the unknown? In addition to the passengers; the ship, the journey, The Mayflower Compact, the early history of the Plymouth Colony and the ubiquitous myths, these all make for fascinating stories.

 Ms. Brayer has a BA from Indiana University and a MA in history and education from Arizona State University. She enjoyed a career in secondary education for 30 years. After retirement, she became a professional genealogist. She is a past president of The Family History Society of Arizona, a member of West Valley Genealogy Society, The Arizona Genealogy Advisory Board, and numerous county societies in Indiana and North Carolina. She has taught genealogy classes and spoken to numerous groups throughout Arizona and the West.

title: Whistler by Ann Patchett [OPTION 2]
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
***Whistler*** by Ann Patchett. If you rely on library copies, reserve ASAP as there's a long wait list. \*\**We're scheduling this book early in the month - 2nd and 3rd Sat. - to avoid Thanksgiving weekend.\*\**

PUBLISHER'S DESCRIPTION: "When Daphne Fuller and her husband Jonathan visit the Metropolitan Museum of Art, they notice an older, white-haired gentleman following them. The man turns out to be Eddie Triplett, her former stepfather, who had been married to her mother for a little more than year when Daphne was nine. Now 53, Daphne hasn’t seen Eddie for many years, not since the fateful event that changed the direction of both their lives. Meeting again, time falls away; while their relationship was brief, it had a profound impact on them both, and now that they are reunited, they have no intention of ever being separated again.

"*Whistler* is a story about two adults looking back over the choices they made, and the choices that were made for them. It’s a story about bravery, memory, the often small yet consequential moments that define our lives, and the endless stream of loss that in time comes for us all. Beautiful in its simplicity, it is ultimately about how love endures, and how the feeling of being known by one other person, even for a short period of time, can change everything."

"This exquisite writer has once again delivered an incandescent work of fiction — sweet, but never sentimental, infinitely wise and suffused with love. It’s also an ode to New York City itself…. While Patchett has clearly drawn on actual events and individuals to produce this luminous work, she exhibits the expert novelist’s knack for following a plot where the imagination takes it.... I didn't want it to end." - Leigh Haber, ***The Los Angeles Times***

“Ann Patchett’s new novel is a rare phenomenon in contemporary fiction: a novel both majestic and intimate, original and masterful in its structure, crystalline in its prose, revelatory in its insights, utterly devastating yet ultimately uplifting in its emotional impact. . . . I think it is her best novel yet.” - Priscilla Gilman, ***The Boston Globe***

"Ann Patchett’s new novel, *Whistler*, is that loveliest of summer gifts, a story of reconciliation, of old affections renewed, of a family’s circumference enlarged. Fans of the author’s previous work will open these pages like an old shoebox of family photos. Newcomers — how I envy them those first moments — will discover a writer of gentle wit and quiet grace." - **Ron Charles**

**Christine**: "Just finished listening to this book and absolutely loved it! If you are interested, please listen to the Audible, read by Patchett, who is an excellent narrator. I've already recommended it to a number of friends. BIG thumbs' up! Would definitely read it again."

**Nancy S**: "I liked *Whistler* a lot. Mostly it hit some personal spots with characters just like people I know and situations I have been in. It is Anne Patchett in her most comfortable place— family type relationships, reevaluated, and transformed and just about always for the better."

title: Booked & Bottled: Build a Blind Date with a Book at Coursey Graves
description:
Taste your way to a book you’ve never read: Coursey Graves pours a flight of wines, each one paired to a genre, and the pour you love points you toward your blind date with a book.

Chardonnay points toward historical fiction, Sonoma Coast Pinot Noir toward romantasy, Syrah toward contemporary fiction, ‘22 Napa Cabernet toward thriller \(exact pairings may shift slightly by the day of the event\). The books are a curated selection of new releases across all of those genres, so you’ll get a few clues along the way, enough to feel confident you’re walking away with something you’ll genuinely like.

Follow your favorite pour to its genre, then build your blind date: choose from book-themed baubles \(bookmarks, stickers, tea, and more\) to tuck inside, wrap it all up yourself, and add a pairing card explaining why that book and that wine belong together. The book itself stays a mystery until you’re home and ready to unwrap it.

Your ticket includes a full glass of wine plus your flight of pours, food from Coursey Graves, your wrapped blind-date book and baubles to take home, fun bookish games, and a spot at the book swap. Add-on blind dates are available if you want to build a second one! One bookish blind date is good, but it also makes a great holiday gift for someone else on your list.

Coursey Graves’ standard tasting runs $75. For $60, this ticket gets you wine, food, access to a great community of readers, a book matched to your favorite pour, and an afternoon built around all four.

$60 general admission, $45 for Novel Pairings Book Club or Coursey Graves Wine Club members. Only 50 tickets available. Come solo, bring a friend, or round up your book club; most people leave having swapped recommendations with someone new. 21\+.

Venice, early 18th century. Renowned for its exceptional music program, the Pièta orphanage is home to Cecilia, a 20-year-old violin virtuoso. Though he cites bass virtuoso Geddy Lee of Rush, and the experimental group The Residents as his greatest influence, Claypool is known to use various styles in his playing, Claypool mixes finger-tapping, flamenco-like strumming, and a Larry Graham-like slap technique to develop his own unique style.  Claypool has earned respect as one of Rock's premier bass talents and has become an influence on younger bassists in recent years. He has played with other artists such as Tom Waits and Buckethead.

title: David Dondero Music & Virgil Shaw
description:
David Dondero, an American troubadour, was born in Duluth, Minnesota in 1969. His love of music began with folk rock and country of the early 70’s and evolved to include punk rock and hip hop of the 80’s. He spent his formative years in suburban Chicago and northern New Jersey listening to pirate radio and heavy metal. As a young man, music molded Dondero’s life. 

Dondero began writing songs in the late 80’s while at Clemson. Initially a drummer and lyricist, he formed Sunbrain in 1991. A post-punk indie rock quartet heavily influenced by Donovan and Fugazi. Sunbrain was signed by Grass Records and they recorded 3 albums. When the group disbanded he went on to play drums for the folk punk band, This Bike is a Pipe Bomb. After 2 years he left the band and began his solo career. He’s been touring for thirty years and his music has taken him around the world multiple times.

His style and ongoing narratives are hard to fit into a particular genre. The music is inspired by heartbreak, hopefulness, everyday work and his never ending tour of life.  Dondero’s lyrics are influenced by the angst of Black Flag, the wanderlust of Bruce Springsteen, the sentimentality of Paul Simon and the politics of Woody Guthrie. 

He’s shared bills and tours with Pedro the Lion, The Mountain Goats, Darren Hanlon, Daniel Johnston and Against Me! In 2006 Bob Boilen and Robin Hilton of NPR put David on their list of the top ten greatest living songwriters. Aside from multiple years at South by Southwest, he was invited by Mudhoney as a featured artist at All Tomorrow’s Parties in Rye, England. God Speed You Black Emperor brought him to The Sled Island Festival in Calgary. And he played the Bellow Winter Music Festival in Australia under the recommendation of Australian songwriter Darren Hanlon. 

He has split seven inches with Mischief Brew and the Pine Hill Haints. Dondero has recorded ten albums and his 11th is slated to come out on Fluff and Gravy Records in Summer of 2023. Recorded in Portland at Fluff and Gravy Studio. Dondero calls Portland, Santa Cruz and Pensacola home and is about to publish his first novel.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Meeting
description:
Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.

In OA, members experience spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery by practicing the Twelve Steps and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

Overeaters Anonymous \(OA\) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person meetings at 9:30 on Sunday mornings at Church of the Nazarene, 18980 Arnold Drive, Sonoma, CA \(a small room directly off of parking lot; look for the sign posted\) and newcomers are always welcome.

You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

OA is not a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does not endorse any specific food plan. 

Visit: https://www.northbayoa.org/

Find a meeting: https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design
location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Maple Magic & Winter Wonder
description:

From the first signs of autumn in October to the brilliant display of rare Asian maples in November and the quiet beauty of early winter in December, each visit offers something new to discover. 

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. Throughout the season, the Garden offers guided walks, hands-on workshops, lectures, and special experiences inspired by the changing landscape. Wander among vibrant fall foliage, breathe in the sweet fragrance of katsura trees, enjoy creative programs, and experience the peaceful beauty of the Garden as it transitions into winter.

title: Jack London Gravesite Memorial
location: Jack London State Historic Park - Event venues (overall park limit)
description:
Jack London died of kidney failure on Nov. 22, 1916. In his short life he accomplished much, not only as a writer of fifty books, but also as an adventurer, reporter, war correspondent, sports article writer, and innovative farmer. He was in the process of developing a model ranch, destined to be the finest in California, when he died. He would have wished farming to be his true legacy, far beyond writing. Learn more about the gravesite.

On the 110th anniversary of his passing - Nov. 22, 2026 - Volunteer Park Historian Lou Leal will preside over a service at London’s gravesite.  Songwriter and vocalist Jeff Falconer will perform his original song, written in memory of Jack London.

The memorial is open to the public at no charge. The park entry fee of $15 per vehicle applies.  Those attending should gather at the House of Happy Walls Museum at 10:30 a.m. to start the half mile walk to the grave site.  A golf cart will be available for those who need assistance.

In the event of rain, the memorial will be held on the second floor in the museum which can only be reached by stairway.  For information about accessibility, call 707-938-5216.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. title: Art Exhibit: Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Napa Valley College Chorale - "A Hero's Journey"
location: Napa Valley College Performing Arts Center
description:
Every story worth telling begins the same way. Not with a plan. Not with a hero who is ready. 

It begins with a call. 

Joseph Campbell found the same journey running beneath human stories across every culture and every century: the ordinary life disrupted, the threshold crossed, the road that takes everything, the transformation that finally makes the return possible. 

*A Hero’s Journey* is a choral concert built on that arc. Five movements. One story. Music spanning Vivaldi to Rodgers and Hammerstein, a forgotten inscription on a cellar wall in wartime Cologne, a Broadway meditation on hope written for a daughter, ancient liturgy, and a 21st-century voice asking, quietly, what it costs to get dressed and show up. Between movements, students from the NVC Reader’s Theater class give voice to the arc — narrating the journey from call to return. 

The NVC Chorale invites you to make the journey with them — a concert about the rest of us. The ones who weren’t ready. The ones who went anyway.

“The Book of Will” brings to life the chaotic, hilarious, passionate, and mostly true endeavor to compile Shakespeare’s plays into the legendary First Folio!

About the show: Without William Shakespeare, we wouldn’t have literary masterpieces like “Romeo and Juliet.” But without Henry Condell and John Heminges, we would have lost half of Shakespeare’s plays forever! description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

title: Flight Lessons: A Folk Opera by Deborah Crooks
description:
Based on a true story about Peregrine Falcons and humans living at the intersection of wild and urban habitats, "Flight Lessons" is a two-act, multi-character folk opera exploring themes of home, adaptation and recovery. The narrative-in-song follows an urban wildlife biologist who monitors the breeding pair of Peregrine Falcons nesting on a bridge and how their lives intersect with the human inhabitants of the neighborhood after one of the birds is shot.  "Flight Lessons"  draws upon Deborah's experiences studying natural history and raptor conservation and features an ensemble cast including Deborah, Kwame Copeland, Sean Lightholder, Karen Mitchell, Liz Stuart and Mick Shaffer.

“FLIGHT LESSONS is a full, rich story—the heroine’s journey—that takes us into the world of urban birds.…remarkable and moving.”— Alameda Post

title: Boot Juice
description: A band that refuses to be locked into a single genre, Boot Juice finds a sense of freedom in their ability to float from bluesy rock’n’roll to progressive bluegrass and back. Inspired by the likes of Railroad Earth and soulful harmonies of Creedence Clearwater Revival, Boot Juice curates a sound that is uniquely their own, resulting in a layered and dynamic live performance. Boot Juice has been kickin' around the west since 2016, leaving audiences happy, and dance floors sticky. The 7-piece band features electric and acoustic guitars, three vocalists, bass, drums, trumpet and alto saxophone. The band has its heart in Americana songwriting, with a rock’n’roll delivery that gets crowds moving. Boot Juice plays music that will attempt to bring you to the street corner, the river side, or the open highway. They have continued to produce new, interesting music that is hard to put a label on. title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Petaluma's 10th Annual Holiday Food Fair
description:
Mon Nov 23rd 3:00-8:00 An Indoor Farmer's Market - Purchase Directly From Local Artisans & Prepare for the Holidays!

holidayfoodfair.com for a list of vendors

Mon Nov 23rd 3:00 to 8:00: \(The Monday before Thanksgiving\) The Petaluma Holiday Food Fair is an indoor farmer’s market where folks can purchase directly from local food artisans to prepare for thanksgiving and beyond. This year, for the first time, we are hosting our annual event at our distillery \(Barber Lee Spirits\) in downtown Petaluma, where fair attendees will also have the opportunity to taste our spirits and enjoy seasonal cocktails and libations while they shop and enjoy our extensive holiday decorations!

FREE tickets and reservations are required, and will book your timeslot for entry.

Kids do not require tickets.

After the 2017 wildfires devastated Sonoma County, Lorraine & Michael Barber of the Brutal Hill Winery noticed that many of the local artisans they supported in their tasting room were suffering from lack of business. At the height of harvest season, farmers markets were closed and sales were slim. They organized this event to get a much needed financial boost to local food producers. The event has become a vital start to the holiday season and remains an important and beloved event for local food artisans and Sonoma County residents to kick off the holiday season!

Sampling is up to the discretion of the individual vendors. Beer, Wine, Cocktails, and Non-Alcoholic drinks will be available for consumption onsite. The number of people allowed in at one time is limited. Tickets are free and include a time preference \(15 minute increments\) so there’s less of a wait and some more space. Kids do not require tickets!

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Mondays
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? Salsa lessons in Marin will help you to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

What You’ll Learn

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

• The Cross Body Lead \(CBL\) Series: Master both Inside and Outside Turns, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

• The “I Turn – You Turn”: A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

• The Walk-Through: Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

• Footwork & Shine: We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

Technique & Artistry

• Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

• The Frame: Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

• Upper Body Mechanics: Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

• Connection: Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

Important Details

• No dance experience required: Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

• No partner necessary: Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

• Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

title: Janice Gould's This Music: Record of a Poet Becoming
description: Two of the book's editors-Kim Shuck \(Cherokee\), former San Francisco Poet Laureate, essayist and fiber artist; and Jennifer Foerster \(Mvskoke\), published poet, arts administrator, and professor-present this many-layered work. This Music is a vital contribution to Indigenous and LGBTQ\+ literatures, offering readers a rare and powerful account of gender, sexuality, and Native identity in mid-century and contemporary America. This work honors Gould's legacy while expanding the canon of poetic memoir. Ideal for readers of poetry, memoir, and Indigenous literature, this book will resonate deeply with anyone drawn to stories of resilience, creativity, and the enduring power of memory. Other editors ofThis Musicare Deborah Miranda, enrolled Ohlone, poet, and author of the iconicBad Indians: A Tribal Memoir; Lisa Tatonetti, Kansas State University professor and author; and Marie-Elise Wheatwind. This Music is from the is from the  University of Arizona Press .

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design
location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Let’s Tap! Beginner - Advanced on Tuesdays
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Welcome to the wonderful world of Tap!
These classes are for those who wish to discover tap dance and those who wish to continue exploring.
This class offering is weekly on Tuesdays in six-week sessions. Three levels are taught: Beginner from 10:15-11 AM, Intermediate from 11 AM - 12 Noon and Advanced from 12:30-1:30 PM. Summer Session starts Tuesday, September 8th and ends Tuesday, October 13. Additional classes can be taken on the same day for $5/class (pay on site).
Classes are led by
Starr Hergenrather and Gabe Copeland
. A limited supply of
tap shoes is available for use at the class.
Please contact us ahead of time to ensure we have the right size for you.
Participation fee is $120 for the series (six sessions), $90 for OCA members.
You can
email us
with any questions, or come to a class.
Register
Tap Dance provides an avenue for developing coordination, balance, musicality, rhythm, and general love for movement. We will learn the basics (if a beginner) and beyond, through warm-ups, discover the language of tap dance, learn the Shim Sham, and routines that will launch you onto your own exploration of the dance form.
Tap is an extremely fun and rewarding form of dance. Tap Dance originated in the 19th century through a fusion of African and Irish dance styles, becoming a unique American art form in the melting pot of New York City. It developed through percussive footwork, initially on plantations and in urban cellars, and later gained widespread popularity through minstrel shows, vaudeville, and Hollywood musicals. Innovators like
Bill "Bojangles" Robinson
, the
Nicholas Brothers
, Eleanor Powell, Fred Astaire, Gene Kelly to name just a few, who shaped its evolution, which continues today with new fusions in contemporary dance.
May 26
, Bojangle’s birthday, is National
Tap Dance Day.
Starr Hergenrather
has been teaching Theatre and Dance for over 54 years, dancing for 70 years, which is amazing since she is only 45 years old! She received her Theatre Arts and Teaching Credentials in 1971 from Denver, CO. Starr has taught theatre/creative dramatics/improvisation/dance to all ages and directed and produced theatre for many, many years. She and her family moved to Sebastopol in 1983. In 1987, she received her Dance credential and degree from SSU. Starr loves the theatre and dance and everything about them. She has performed on stage and in film throughout her teaching career. Before joining the staff at Analy in 2001 where she became the Theatre Arts Program Director and taught one dance class starting in 2010, when the high school lost its Dance instructor due to No Child Left Behind, she taught at Brookhaven School from 1990-2001 teaching a myriad of subjects, including Theatre and Dance, and Rincon Valley Junior High School from 1987-1997, as BJ Van Noy’s choreographer and asst. director of her Music Program. Starr’s tap mentor was a Vaudeville and later Broadway song and Dance man by the name of Jack Williams. Starr studied with Jack for almost 20 years., until his waning years.
Tap, which is a magical form of dance, btw, is Starr’s first dance love, next to swing, salsa, and partner dancing, and then just plain social, wild hippie dancing at concerts.
Starr also teaches Private Tap Lessons for any level dancer. Starr has a studio at her home.
Gabe Copeland (pictured with Mindy on flier above)
Gabe has been a dance educator for over 20 years. He has performed nationally and internationally as a featured member of the Los Angeles based touring company Rhapsody in Taps. Other credits include ABC’s Gong Show, China’s Dream television show, soloist in KIN Dance Company’s Down Around Brown Town and soloist on an international tour with Caution: Men At Work Tap! He has also performed in many Southern California Civic Light Opera productions such as Cole, Crazy For You, and Rodgers & Hart: A Celebration. Most recently, Gabe performed in the critically acclaimed Jazz Tap Jam! Show for the Lively Arts Foundation honoring Gregory Hines and had the privilege of performing a piece originally choreographed by the tap legend himself.
Mindy Copeland
As a dance educator since 1995, Mindy has also enjoyed a career in performance. As a member of the Los Angeles based touring company, Rhapsody in Taps, Mindy performed the choreography of Linda Sohl-Ellison, Gregory Hines, Fred Strickler, Sam Weber, Brenda Bufalino and Foster Johnson. She was a featured soloist in the international tour of Caution: Men At Work Tap! Mindy appeared in the short film, Tap Heat with choreography by Danny Daniels, and appeared in and choreographed for national and international television shows including the Jerry Lewis Telethon, China’s Dream Show, Spain’s Extremo Urbano, and ABC’s Gong Show. Other stage credits include, appearing with the legendary Chester Whitmore in A Tribute to Jeni Le Gon, and KIN Dance Company’s James Brown tribute show, Down Around Brown Town. Most recently, Mindy directed and performed in the critically acclaimed 2023 Jazz Tap Jam! Show for the Lively Arts Foundation.
The Copelands
have shared the stage with tap legends Dianne Walker, Arthur Duncan, Fayard Nicholas and Bob Carroll and performed Begin the Beguine together in Swing Into Spring. They direct
Tap Overload
which has a collection of original tap dance ﬁlm shorts on its YouTube channel and produced an original tap dance comedy show-
Office Beat.
The show received rave reviews and the official Hollywood Fringe Festival Award, Best of Physical theatre and Dance as well as the Robby Award for Best Choreography of LA Theatre in 2016.

This is a social, feel-good outdoor experience designed for anyone looking for something a little different to do after dark—part nature, part adventure, part pure vibe.

$60 per person includes everything: • Hobie pedal kayak • PFD and safety lights • Experienced local guide • A memorable, moonlit river experience

✨ Easy. Playful. Peaceful. Spend your evening under the full moon—on the water.

description:
Jewish Wisdom for a Life That Matters

No matter how much we achieve, something within us still asks: “Is this it? Isn’t there something more?”

The Kabbalah of Meaning is a new six-session JLI course exploring the Jewish answer to that question. What are we really searching for—and where can it be found?

Drawing on Kabbalah and centuries of Jewish wisdom, we’ll uncover the essential building blocks of a deeply meaningful life. We’ll explore how purpose can be found in our work, relationships, challenges, accomplishments, and even the ordinary routines that fill our days.

You don’t have to revamp your life. You don’t need to meditate on a mountaintop. You simply need a new lens through which to see the rich world of meaning already woven into every part of your life.

Thoughtful, practical, and surprisingly relevant, this course offers fresh perspectives and useful tools for living with greater clarity, connection, and intention.

Try 1st class free.

No previous Jewish learning required. Come as you are—and bring your questions.

title: Intermediate Salsa Class
description:
This class is designed for dancers who have a solid grasp of the basics and are eager to expand their repertoire with more complex and fluid movements.

Turns and Spins:

Intricate Patterns:

Learn to execute the 360, wrap, as well as various Cross Body Lead variations like the U-Turn and Spiral.

Footwork and Styling:

Enhance your rhythm and flair with advanced footwork like the Suzy Q, Front Tap, and Mambo Step. We’ll also work on styling with a wrap and improving your posture and upper body movement.

This class is your chance to refine your technique, improve your lead-follow connection, and add a variety of fun and dynamic moves to your salsa vocabulary. Join us and elevate your dance!

As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

program overview

The “Julia” Soda Firing Club is designed for folks looking for longterm use with our Soda Kiln, Julia. The club is led by Studio Monitors, and a Studio Technician but involves no formal instruction in soda firing processes. Without a formalized instructor, our Soda Club offers a more financially accessible way of having work soda-fired, without the need to retake our Intro to Soda Firing workshop courses. The Soda Club will run firings monthly or as often as desired and needed depending on participant interest. Unlike our Soda Firing Workshops, club firings will include no instruction on wadding, slips, glazes, or any lectures on the subject of soda firing. As such, participants must feel comfortable with the safety and care of the equipment, as well as loading, firing, and maintenance procedures surrounding the firing process. title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Belly Dancing with Raja - Thursdays
description:
DATE AND TIME: Thursdays, 5:30 PM

Unlock your inner strength and find your flow. Belly dancing with Raja is an innovative fusion class that blends the rhythmic artistry of belly dance with the high-energy benefits of aerobics. Designed to be both a cardiovascular challenge and a deep toning session, this class focuses on the “powerhouse” of the body—your core.

By layering fluid, isolative movements over an athletic aerobic base, you will challenge your muscles in ways traditional gym workouts can’t reach.

What to Expect in Belly Dancing Class

• Core-Centric Power: Use undulations and shimmies to engage deep abdominal muscles for a tighter, stronger midsection.

• Functional Stability: Improve your balance and posture through controlled, hip-driven movements and low-impact aerobic footwork.

• Total Body Toning: Build lean muscle in your legs, glutes, and arms while maintaining a constant, heart-pumping pace.

• Mind-Body Connection: Enhance your coordination and body awareness through rhythmic, expressive choreography.

“Whether you’re looking to define your waistline or simply want a workout that feels like a celebration, this class offers the perfect balance of sweat and grace.”

Difficulty Level: All levels welcome! No prior dance experience is required—just bring your energy and a willingness to move.

description:
Your First Steps into Bachata

This class is perfect for bachata beginners that want to learn basic steps and skills, or those who want to refresh their foundational skills. We understand that learning something new can feel a little intimidating. That’s why our supportive and relaxed environment is specifically designed to make learning bachata basics an absolute blast!

Our friendly instructors will guide you through:

**Basic directional steps:** You’ll learn the fundamental movements that form the building blocks of all bachata dancing.

**Proper frame for partner work:** Discover how to connect comfortably and effectively with a partner, setting you up for smooth and enjoyable dances.

**Simple turn patterns:** We’ll introduce you to easy-to-follow turn patterns that will have you dancing with a partner in no time.

We’ve carefully organized our curriculum to ensure that each movement is easy to grasp and remember, building your confidence with every step. Our goal is to make learning fun. Join us to learn Bachata in Marin.

Important Details

**No dance experience required:** Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

**No partner necessary:** Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

Please wear **non-marking shoe soles:** This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

Come join us and discover the joy of bachata! We can’t wait to see you on the dance floor.

title: Samba no Pé
description:

The Basic Step: You will master the signature quick-quick-slow rhythm that defines Samba no Pé.

Arm & Hip Styling: You will learn how to add the authentic flair, movement, and energy that makes Brazilian samba so captivating.

Technique & Posture: You will receive tips on proper body alignment to help you dance longer, faster, and more safely.

title: Gain Speaking Confidence with Mare Island Toastmasters
description:
We meet in-person only on the 1st and 2nd Thursdays of the month. However, you can catch us online every Thursday unless the meeting date falls on a holiday.

Please register at https://signup.com/go/WiniixA

What is Toastmasters About?

Usually at our meetings, we will have a prepared speech, and a speech evaluation. The Grammarian and Wizard of Ah's will listen for turns of phrases and the use of filler words. We also practice impromptu speaking during the section of the meeting called Table Topics. During Table Topics, at a recent meeting, we were asked what we felt was the biggest communication problem or challenge. What would you answer in a fast moment? Table topics will challenge you to think quickly and give an answer without preparation.

You will also hear tips on public speaking skills at our upcoming meeting. Whether you're a seasoned traveler or just looking for some adventure from the comfort of your home, this event is perfect for you.

Toastmasters International is all about communication excellence, and for 100 years and counting, Toastmasters have been expressing themselves better, practicing, and evaluating in a fun club environment, shining all around the world.

To find out more--Msg us on our webpage \(under Contact Us\) button at

https://mareisland.toastmastersclubs.org/

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

Shut Up & Write!® Wine Country
**This event is hosted on the Shut Up & Write website, so please [sign up here](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2me5JeN600/id2w10OBEA00) for your writing event.**

**ABOUT THE EVENT**
Join us virtually for an hour + of writing using Zoom. Let's keep together as much as we can during these uncertain times and keep on writing. Look for the schedule online and join us.

We’ve discovered that it’s strikingly helpful to write with other writers. See if it’s true for you at 3pm on Friday afternoon. Be it a book, blog, script, essay, dissertation, resume, melody, poem or just plain work stuff, you are invited to write it with us. No one will see what you've written or give you unsolicited advice. Instead of just thinking about writing, come and get some real writing done.

JOIN US!

1. Link available on the Shut Up and Write website..

Please note:

1. If you don't have Zoom set up on your computer yet, leave 15-30 minutes ahead of time to get it set up!
2. If you have difficulty with audio (don't have a microphone set up), as long as you have a speaker, you can call in (you'll see phone numbers when you log in).
3. If you are late, you won't be able to intro with us, but you are still welcome to join in.
4. If you won't be able to make it, please cancel so that the space is available to another writer.

SCHEDULE:
3:00 - quick intros.
around 3:10 - timer starts: write for 70 mins.
4:20 - (the end) wrap up

Wherever you are, we hope to see you online! Keep on writing...
Regards,
Lorraine Segal

description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on first, second and fourth **Saturdays of the month from 9:45 - 10:15 AM at** ​**Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin, 240 Channing Way, San Rafael CA 94903**. Contact: Sue M. 415-298-6792​. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan. 

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

with Djuna Devereaux and Rolf Gates

In this daylong retreat, we’ll cultivate embodied presence as a taproot—grounding us and settling the mind. From this refuge, we’ll explore opening to clarity, joy, and belonging.

Our day will weave together Dharma teachings, meditation, somatic movement, and yoga asana into a deeply nourishing experience. We’ll begin with floor-based movement to release tension and fatigue, then flow into accessible yoga sequences. Drawing on personal stories and classical Buddhist teachings, we’ll explore what it means to be grounded in the body, held by awareness, and supported by community. All abilities and levels of experience warmly welcomed!

Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Saturdays
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? You’ve mastered the basics, now it’s time to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

**What You’ll Learn**

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

**• The Cross Body Lead (CBL) Series:** Master both **Inside and Outside Turns**, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

**• The “I Turn – You Turn”:** A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

**• The Walk-Through:** Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

**• Footwork & Shine:** We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

**Technique & Artistry**

Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

**• The Frame:** Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

**• Upper Body Mechanics:** Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

**• Connection:** Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

**Important Details**

**• No dance experience required:** Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

**• No partner necessary:** Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

**•** Please wear **non-marking shoe soles:** This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

Date & Time:

**Thursdays 7:30 PM**

**Saturday 11:00 AM**

Instructor: Lucie Ebnerova

Address: 4140 Redwood Highway #8 San Rafael, CA

Note: Arrive 10 minutes before. No floor marking shoe soles allowed.

Join us for line dancing lessons from Grapevine Dance! Plus live music from Dustin Saylor & The Stowaways.

About Dustin Saylor:

Dustin Saylor, a Northern California-born country singer-songwriter, has made a name for himself as the #1 Country/Folk artist in the San Francisco Bay Area. His musical journey began in childhood, first at the piano and later as a guitarist and singer for his high school youth group and local church. Despite early challenges, including a devastating American Idol rejection in 2009, Saylor had a transformative moment on his long drive home, realizing that true success required full commitment. Embracing his calling, he quit bartending, pursued a music degree at Sonoma State University, and became a full-time musician. Over the years, he has performed alongside artists like Tyler Rich, Chase Rice, and Daughtry, with his sound often compared to Thomas Rhett and Chris Stapleton. His songwriting is deeply personal, shaped by his early experiences of adoption and the contrasting struggles and joys of his life. Through his music, Saylor seeks to inspire, heal, and create a space where people can connect beyond labels. Committed to his craft, he remains "all in," determined to sing and play music for the rest of his life.

description:
This holiday season, Spreckels Theatre Company offers a heartwarming alternative to traditional seasonal fare with *Rooted*, a story about the messy, fierce love that keeps us grounded. An intelligent, gentle comedy by Deborah Zoe Laufer, *Rooted* plays Nov. 27 – Dec.13!

Emery is perfectly content living in her beloved treehouse, completely isolated from the world, communing with her plants. Meanwhile, down on the ground, her sister Hazel is thoroughly miserable, slaving away at a dead-end diner job just to survive and financially support Emery’s eccentric lifestyle. Looking on from the sidelines, Luanne is yearning for something, anything to bring true meaning into her life.

﻿The sisters' fragile ecosystem is completely upended when Emery’s YouTube videos documenting her plant experiments unexpectedly go viral. Almost overnight, her digital musings accidentally incite a full-blown CULT(!). As throngs of devoted truth-seekers congregate below the treehouse, the lives of all three women are plunged into chaos, compelling each woman to choose their own path and find their bliss.

title: Moonalice
description:
Moonalice is a psychedelic, roots-rock band of seasoned musicians mixing a variety of genres with extended musical improvisations that evoke a sense of adventure and exploration. Everyone is a part of the experience and the music inspires dancing and other acts of self expression. Every show has an original art poster created by a well-known artist memorializing that event and given to all attendees…each poster has its own Moonalice legend. All concerts are broadcasted live in HD and available in archive shortly after their set.

Moonalice plays mostly original material mixed with several covers, and during their extended freeform jams the band moves as one, drawing from many musical genres honed from years of experience playing with various major acts. Their single "It's 4:20 Somewhere" has been downloaded over 6 million times. Just released: 420 Gathering of the Tribe by Jay Blakesberg and Alex Fischer – a short film about the Moonalice posters and poster artists: http://www.moonalice.com/song/its-420-somewhere. Social media: nearly 424,000 on Facebook & over 67,000 on Twitter. Their extensive tour schedule and videos of every Moonalice show can be seen at moonalice.com and every show poster with legends can be viewed at moonaliceposters.com.

Band

Dylan Chambers: Vocals, Cowbell \(Midnight Transit, The New Chambers Brothers\)

Lester Chambers: Vocals, Harmonica \(Chambers Brothers, The New Chambers Brothers\)

Jason Crosby: Keyboards \(Phil Lesh, Terrapin Family Band, Jenny Lewis, John McLaughlin, Robert Randolph, Blind Boys of Alabama, Susan Tedeschi\)

Roger McNamee: Rhythm Guitar, Vocals, Bass. \(Guff, The Engineers, Random Axes, Flying Other Brothers\)

John Molo: Drums, Vocals. \(Bruce Hornsby & The Range, John Fogerty, Phil Lesh & Friends, The Other Ones, David Nelson Band\).

Pete Sears: Bass, Keyboards, Guitar, Vocals \(Sam Gopal Dream, Rod Stewart, Jefferson Starship, Jerry Garcia, Hot Tuna, John Lee Hooker, David Nelson Band, Phil Lesh & Friends\).

Barry Sless: Lead Guitar, Pedal Steel Guitar, Bass. \(Phil Lesh & Friends, David Nelson Band, Kingfish, Cowboy Jazz\).

Chloe Tietjen: Vocals \(T Sisters\)

Erika Tietjen: Vocals, Guitar \(T Sisters\)

Rachel Tietjen: Vocals, Guitar \(T Sisters\)

Fun facts

Moonalice’s first show was in May, 2007.

Moonalice’s single, “It’s 4:20 Somewhere” has been downloaded more than 5 million times.

Moonalice invented the Twittercast concert, broadcasting links in near real time for live concerts and at random times for past shows. The band has done 103 Twittercast concerts.

Moonalice is the first band to Mooncast live video of all of its concerts. Moonalice has broadcast nearly ever concert since 2010, the first band to operate a satellite-based broadcast system that enables High Definition live video to smartphones and iPads WITHOUT an app!

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Meeting
description:

In OA, members experience spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery by practicing the Twelve Steps and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

Overeaters Anonymous \(OA\) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person meetings at 9:30 on Sunday mornings at Church of the Nazarene, 18980 Arnold Drive, Sonoma, CA \(a small room directly off of parking lot; look for the sign posted\) and newcomers are always welcome.

You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

OA is not a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does not endorse any specific food plan.

title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design
location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: The Women of Jack London's Beauty Ranch: Hands That Shaped the Vision
location: Jack London State Historic Park - Oak Grove Picnic Area (standing capacity)
description:
In honor of Charmian London’s birthday on November 27, join a walk celebrating her legacy and recognizing the many women whose lives, work, and creativity have helped shape the history, culture, and landscape of the park.

In the five short years Jack London lived at Beauty Ranch, he imagined it on a grand scale. That vision took root and endured through the labor, intelligence, and perseverance of two key women, Charmian Kittredge London and Eliza Shepard — who stewarded the dream, land, and legacy through upheaval and change, long after Jack London was gone. This two-hour tour of Beauty Ranch and the House of Happy Walls Museum invites visitors to step into their stories and discover how a vision became an enduring reality.

Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

title: Laurie Lewis and the Right Hands
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Bluegrass and American Roots Music
Don't miss this incredible show at OCA! Bluegrass legend Laurie Lewis and her amazing band The RIght Hands will give us an afternoon show that you won't soon forget. Laurie will be joined by Brandon Godman, Hasee Ciaccio and other fine musicians for this performance.
Tickets are $35, $30 for OCA members. Doors open at 2:30 PM. Refreshments available, free parking. Art gallery open during intermission. ADA seating available - please contact us at
info@occidentalcenterforthearts.org
for details.
Get Tickets
For nearly four decades, Laurie Lewis has gathered fans and honors for her powerful and emotive voice and her versatile, dynamic songwriting. She is a sought-after recording producer and an equally skilled teacher and mentor.
And she is an inspiration and a ground-breaker – across genres, across geography and across gender barriers.
Laurie has shown us how a woman can blend into any part of the classic bluegrass singing trio, and she showed us how a great voice could move fluidly between bluegrass and other types of music. She showed us how a female fiddler could emulate the strength and grit of the early bluegrass musicians. She has shown how a Californian can appeal to traditional bluegrass audiences, as well as winning acclaim in the worlds of Americana and folk music.
She has shown us how to lead bands of talented musicians – learning from them while helping them make their best music. And she has shown us how to thrive in a constantly changing musical environment – without ever sacrificing her art.
"Her voice is a rare combination of grit and grace, strength and delicacy. Her stories always ring true."

**Larry Vuckovich** is a **Yugoslavian-born American jazz pianist** acclaimed for his eclectic style blending bop, post-bop, blues, and world music. Classically trained in Kotor, he emigrated to San Francisco in 1951, studied with Vince Guaraldi, and performed with legends like Mel Tormé, Jon Hendricks, Philly Joe Jones, and Dexter Gordon.
