Poetic Medicine in Community: Healing Through Creativity and ConnectionTuesday, December 8th, 4:00-5:30pm Class Description: Poetry can be a salve for the heart and soul. It is a way of speaking what is true in our hearts and is often difficult to access without a creative spark. You do not have to be a “poet” or even a “writer” to allow words and feeling to your through your pen. COME JOIN US!Writing poetry in community is a bit like attending a meditation retreat. The instruction for most beginners when learning to meditate is to simply bring oneself back to the breath, each time the mind wanders. In poem-making, the instruction is to bring oneself back to the heart and along with a deep breath, see if one can open a little bit wider. When we witness each other in this process, in a circle of open-heartedness, something magical happens!This is an IN-PERSON gathering in an open and safe creative community. We are all poets! Please bring your own writing materials. 22 students maximum. About the Instructor: Redwing Keyssar has been leading “Poetic Medicine in Community” sessions through her work in Palliative Care at UCSF since 2020. Her work has created an international community of people who, by listening to and writing poetry together, have healed wounds of grief and loss, helped ”wounded healers,” and provided resiliency to move forward on our life paths.Redwing is a Palliative Care nurse, educator and consultant, an end-of-life doula, author, poet, song-writer, ceremonialist, national presenter and frequent contributor to public issues about Palliative and End of Life Care. She is a Board member of the Sebastopol Senior Center and offers presentations about end-of-life issues throughout the Bay Area. Before working at the UCSF MERI CENTER, her professional career included being the Clinical Director at Zen Hospice Project and the Director of Palliative Care and Nursing at Jewish Family and Children’s Services from 2004-2018. She is a founder and adjunct faculty member of the California State University Shiley/Haynes Institute of Palliative Care and has taught courses at OLLI at Sonoma State. Redwing is the author of an award-winning book, “Last Acts of Kindness; Lessons for the Living from the Bedsides of the Dying” and is the recipient of numerous awards in the field of Palliative Care.She is passionate about utilizing poetry as a healing modality!

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

*Maple Magic* *& Winter Wonder* invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. Throughout the season, the Garden offers guided walks, hands-on workshops, lectures, and special experiences inspired by the changing landscape. Wander among vibrant fall foliage, breathe in the sweet fragrance of katsura trees, enjoy creative programs, and experience the peaceful beauty of the Garden as it transitions into winter.

Join us for Abstract Watercolor Painting at Riley Street, Santa Rosa

Instructor: Anne Millett

Date: Tuesday, December 8th

Time: 11:00AM-2:30PM

Fee: $45.00


There will be over 70 high quality paint colors for you to choose from, plus 6 metallics. You will spend time selecting your colors intuitively, for the way they make you feel in the moment. This process is quite personal.

What we paint does not need to accurately represent real things that we see in the "outside world". We listen to our intuitions as our paintings build shape by shape, mark by mark, without planning the end result. We paint simply and methodically, focusing on putting paint on paper and seeing what happens, then where we'll go next.

title: Sound Bath with Laura Benson
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental, CA 95465
description:
Rest & Renew at our Sound Bath!
Support your nervous system, release anxiety and stress, and harmonize your body, mind and spirit on the 2nd Tuesday of every month! Laura Benson has a Masters in Intuition Medicine(R) and is a certified sound healer who will guide you through a gentle meditation before each sound bath session. Bring your own yoga mat & blanket and come ready to rest and renew! In the OCA Studio.
Sliding scale pricing $25-$35.
Register
A sound bath is a whole-body, immersive listening experience. During a sound bath, participants often sit or lie down, and are surrounded by the mostly non-melodic soundscapes created by a range of instruments played by the sound bath facilitator. Hence, they are “bathed” in sound.
Sound therapy is a non-invasive healing modality that utilizes the physical and physiological interactions of sound on our bodies and nervous systems to produce therapeutic results. In a sound healing session, specific sonic frequencies are used to soothe the central nervous system, calm the breath, and quiet the mind by encouraging the brain to move into more relaxed states, down from beta (fight-or-flight) and into theta and alpha waves. This increases present-moment awareness and reduces stress and anxiety. Sound baths have been found to be effective in improving mood, cognitive function, and overall mental, physical, and spiritual wellbeing.
Crystal bowl sound baths are particularly powerful in that each bowl is tuned to a specific frequency that corresponds with a different chakra, or energy center, of the body. Based on specific needs, a practitioner can focus on releasing tension or clearing out stuck energy in specific chakras by playing certain bowls or intervals.
While attending a sound bath, you may experience physical sensations brought out by the crystal sound bowls or gong, such as tingling in your limbs or scalp, slowing of your breathing, eye flutters, or small muscle spasms. Not to worry! These sensations often indicate the release of tension or emotional energy stored in the body’s energy systems.

title: Take the art of Still Life to new places
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Thursdays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 11:30am - 1:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

title: Introduction to Asemic Writing — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Introduction to Asemic Writing (December 12th)

  
    
      
        
          $175.00
        
      
    
  

Introduction to Asemic Writing Saturday, December 12th, 2026 - 10:00am-4:00pm$160.00 + $15.00 Materials Fee = $175.00 RegistrationClass Limited to 12 StudentsRegister now for both of Sherrie Lovler’s Workshops this weekend, and receive $20.00 off your total order! Use code SHRRLVLR-EARLYBIRD-12121326 until November 12th to claim your discount!December 12th: Introduction to Asemic WritingDecember 13th: Wabi-Sabi Ink Painting: Finding Beauty in ImperfectionClass Description: Asemic writing is the creation of marks that resemble handwriting but carry no literal meaning or readable text. It is the word before words form—the voice too distant to be understood—a universal expression without country or dialect.We’ll begin with a slideshow exploring the rich history and possibilities of asemic writing, from ancient scripts and symbols to the calligraphic line and the work of contemporary artists. From there, you’ll begin your own exploration using ink, watercolor, and a variety of tools on paper.Through guided exercises and playful experimentation, we’ll explore line, gesture, rhythm, repetition, and space. You’ll discover how asemic marks can infiltrate and transform your existing artwork or become works of art in their own right.You’ll leave with a collection of new work, fresh approaches to mark-making, and a deeper trust in your own intuition and expressive voice. My intention is to guide you beyond casual scribbling toward authentic marks—marks that arise from the heart and become uniquely your own.All levels welcome.IMPORTANT: CLICK HERE FOR THE LIST OF REQUIRED MATERIALS FOR THIS CLASS. Not all materials are provided, please see the list of request materials above. If you have any questions regarding materials, please contact your instructor: sherrie@artandpoetry.com—About the Instructor: Sherrie Lovler is a painter, poet, and teacher whose work bridges Western calligraphy and the expressive spirit of Asian brush painting. With a BA in Studio Art, she has taught for several decades at international calligraphy conferences and institutions including Ghost Ranch, Northern Arizona University, and local art centers. Her paintings explore the space between writing and image. Inspired by Asian brushwork and the Japanese aesthetic of wabi-sabi, she embraces imperfection, spontaneity, and fluid mark-making. Sumi ink, gesture, color, and asemic writing become an abstract visual language. She is the author, illustrator, and designer of the award-winning book On Softer Ground. Her latest book, Distant Voices, explores art as a collaboration with nature, poetry, and unseen influences. She participates in Sonoma County Art Trails, Art at the Source, and presented a solo exhibition at Gallery Route One in Point Reyes Station in 2025. www.artandpoetry.com

description:
Award winning singer/songwriter and legendary guitarist join forces for special performance!
Award winning singer/songwriter Keith Greeninger and legendary guitarist Nina Gerber join forces for a powerful night of music, song and community celebration. Both artists share deep roots in the rich California music scene and are well know for their dynamic, improvisational performances and collaborations.
Don't miss this special performance! Tickets are $35 General Admission, $30 for OCA members. We expect this show to sell out so get your tickets early!
Get Tickets
Guitarist
Nina Gerber
started her music career playing along side of the iconic singer songwriter Kate Wolf. She has since gone on to establish herself as one of the finest guitarists on the planet performing and recording with some of the genre’s finest songwriters including Nanci Griffith, Karla Bonoff, Greg Brown, Eliza Gilkyson, Laurie Lewis and Chris Webster just to name a few.
Keith Greeninger
is a compelling singer/songwriter and performer whose songs have won top honors at such prestigious music festivals as the Telluride Bluegrass Festival and the Kerrville Folk Festival. A seasoned troubador who paints intricate portraits of the human condition with powerful melodic images, deep engaging guitar rhythms and compelling, heart-wrenching vocals, his songs cut an honest, hard worn path to places of simple truth about good people holding on to hope and instinct in a world that often tries to strip these things away.

title: Focus Night: Geminids Meteor Shower
description: Move over, summer Perseids. December's Geminid shower is considered the best and most reliable meteor shower of the year. Under dark clear skies, counts can reach 50-100 per hour or more on peak night. But this is only one of many factors that set these meteors apart from all other showers. Their speed and composition create meteors that flare low in the atmosphere, are easier to spot, and leave bright, often yellow, trails. This is one of the very few showers visible all night long. What causes this dazzling display and why does it occur at this time of year? Come learn about these unique meteors, their unusual history, and their mysterious origin. This Focus Night equips you for a Geminid ”peak” experience. Unlike planets that can hang around for months, a meteor shower is only visible over a short period of time. Highest counts will occur later in the night and into the early morning hours. You will learn about different kinds of showers, how best to view them, and how to understand what you are seeing. You’ll also discover factors that influence meteor counts and how to optimize your viewing. Plan to be in the classroom by 6:55PM to ensure you have a good seat. Program begins promptly at 7:00PM . Sales are limited to 40 guests so we can provide a more personal experience. Allow generous time to arrive and park. Please visit https://rfo.simpletix.com for important information and to buy tickets. You MUST have a ticket to attend this event; tickets will not be sold at the door. Cost includes the Sugarloaf Ridge State Park parking fee. Please note that tickets are non-refundable and cannot be used for future events.RFO is operated by the Valley of the Moon Observatory Association, a 501(3)(c) nonprofit organization. All proceeds go toward maintaining this beloved Sonoma County institution.

description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner

title: Give 'Em the Axe! Ladies Night at the Range in Santa Rosa
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
Join us for an axe-throwing session to blow off some steam. I'm super excited to be able to offer a ladies' Axe-throwing night in Santa Rosa. If you've ever had a curiosity about this fun activity, this is your chance to find out more!

We have reserved a group spot with the indoor range on a Wednesday night. It will consist of an introductory lesson, and then we all get to practice taking turns. Everyone will get ample time to practice, as they have many lanes.

This event is focused on a less-competitive, relaxed, and entertaining atmosphere. All skill levels are encouraged. All equipment and targets are provided by them, and we will probably get about 1 to 2 hours to enjoy ourselves.

I encourage everyone to bring a bottle of wine or a snack to share with the rest of the group (We usually end up with a lovely charcuterie and wine spread for everyone to enjoy).

There are 10 spots available, guests welcome. The ladies' group lesson and event is $31 per person, with $6 prepaid via Paypal and $25 paid to the range.

Please only RSVP 'Yes' if you are able to make it, hostess Daima Phipps will be collecting a $6 fee via Paypal to hold your spot. Paypal/Meetup should lead you to make your payment after you RSVP 'Yes'.

Closed-toed shoes are recommended.

There is an attendance policy for all our events: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

Cheers, and hope to see you there!

Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Thursdays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 11:30am - 1:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.

title: Young, Gifted, and Black - Art Submissions Due
description: Young, Gifted, and Black: Art by Black Students at SRJC is an upcoming exhibition at the SRJC Multicultural Museum celebrating the creativity and artistic voices of Black students across campus. Created in recognition of Black History Month, the exhibition provides a dedicated space for Black student artists to have their work seen, valued, and celebrated by the SRJC community.  Black students are invited to submit original artwork in any medium or theme, including visual art, poetry, and other forms of creative writing. Artwork does not need to focus on Black identity or the Black experience—the exhibition celebrates the breadth of Black creativity and the individuality of each participating artist.  The exhibition will be on display in the ground floor library display cases from the beginning of the Spring 2027 semester through Spring Break. Students interested in participating must drop off their work at the SRJC Multicultural Museum by December 18, 2026.Learn more about the museum on the SRJC Multicultural Museum website. title: Yesteryear by Caro Claire Burke (option 1)
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
A modern day Christian tradwife Natalie decides with her husband to take the family to live in a farmhouse, grow their own food, raise chickens and a cow, and raise/home school their ever-increasing brood without modern influences. However -- mom is also a social media influencer who videos everything... except the nannies and farmworkers behind the scenes. She wakes up one day and she and some version of her family are in a real farmhouse (with no helpers) in 1855! How to get out of this nightmare/delusion/time travel?

"I found it to be a realy page turner--couldn't put it down. I definitely think that we should read this for our group. It's so unusual and I think it would provide fodder for very interesting discussion." - Nancy R.

"For the life of me, I can’t figure out why I kept reading this book given that most of the characters in it are deplorable. But I sure kept reading it. And then when I finished it, I wondered what kind of a person could write such a book and I was surprised when I listened to the interview that the author is actually full-fledged human being with a heart and a sense of humor. To me, that the sign of someone with tremendous craft. There are many topics in this book that I think would be a wealth for us to discuss: The double lives of social media influencers, Tradwife vs Girlboss, can we go back into the way that used to be. I suspect the reason this book is so hot because it’s so topical." - Lucinda

"It took me a bit to get into (I was just so annoyed at the beginning:) but after things began to develop, I was hooked. A lot to discuss - although it may be tough to separate out discussion on the book itself and the real-world implications!" - Debra

"[Why You Should Read ‘Yesteryear’ Now](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/10/briefing/yesteryear-caro-claire-burke.html?unlocked_article_code=1.01A.Gak9.SZGpJviEJq74&smid=url-share)" - NY Times

"‘[Yesteryear’ is this summer’s must-discuss book. We have questions.](https://www.washingtonpost.com/style/interactive/2026/06/18/yesteryear-is-this-summers-must-read-book-let-discuss/)" - Washington Post:

title: Fresh Pressed Flower Card Workshop
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Jan Lochner
Date: Saturday, December 19th
Time: 2:00PM-5:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Fee: $40.00

This is a hands-on make and take class where you will make at least five items including a bookmark, a greeting card, a fridge magnet and an ornament. The class will use two different techniques and Jan will explain how to press flowers and which flowers hold their color best. It is a creative experience!


To register for this workshop, please contact Jan at: mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com

Creating note cards from pressed flowers has been Jan’s hobby for 25 years, though she has no formal art training. She utilizes color,
shape and texture on fine quality paper, each card uniquely handmade. Jan’s home in Sebastopol is her studio: the dining room table is her workshop, the kitchen cupboards storing boxes and trays of flowers. She buys card stock by the thousand and picks blooms from her garden and other public places. Her family is used to me saying, “could we stop for just a few minutes so I can gather some… ”

It is a wonderful way of life.

description:
Sips and Stars ~ an evening of fine wine and cosmic wonder.

Join us for a magical night under the stars at the Robert Ferguson Observatory! Our Sips & Stars event blends the beauty of the night sky with the elegance of Sonoma County wine. Enjoy a curated tasting experience hosted by Burtech Family Vineyard,  while taking in breathtaking views of the cosmos through our powerful telescopes.

As twilight falls, relax with a glass of wine in hand and listen to engaging astronomy talks from our knowledgeable docents. Once darkness settles, step up to the observatory’s telescopes for guided viewing of planets, star clusters, and distant galaxies.

Whether you’re a wine lover, stargazer, or simply looking for a unique evening out in Sonoma Valley, Sips & Stars promises an unforgettable experience where earthly pleasures meet celestial beauty.

description:
Instructor: Jan Lochner
Date: Sunday, December 20th
Time: 2:00PM-5:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Fee: $40.00

This is a hands-on make and take class where you will make at least five items including a bookmark, a greeting card, a fridge magnet and an ornament. The class will use two different techniques and Jan will explain how to press flowers and which flowers hold their color best. It is a creative experience!


To register for this workshop, please contact Jan at: mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com

Creating note cards from pressed flowers has been Jan’s hobby for 25 years, though she has no formal art training. She utilizes color,
shape and texture on fine quality paper, each card uniquely handmade. Jan’s home in Sebastopol is her studio: the dining room table is her workshop, the kitchen cupboards storing boxes and trays of flowers. She buys card stock by the thousand and picks blooms from her garden and other public places. Her family is used to me saying, “could we stop for just a few minutes so I can gather some… ”

It is a wonderful way of life.

*A note to all students: Please park on in the East facing parking lot while attending classes. We greatly appreciate it. Thank you.

description:
Full Circle Studio - Creative Arts
**Wise Woman Sanctuary, A Safe Place for Women to Explorate Through Image**

Step into a transformative space where for women to delve into **self-exploration, art therapy**, and mindfulness come together to nurture your inner wisdom. At **Wise Women Sanctuary**, we invite you to engage in **Personal Exploration Through Image**, using creativity as a pathway to connect with your inner self.

This **Creative Expression Workshop** blends **painting, meditation**, and holistic wellness practices to deepen your **self-awareness** and inspire **self-empowerment**. Guided by Christi Corradi, a seasoned mentor in **manifestation** and the **Universal Principles**, you’ll uncover new tools for personal growth and gain profound insights into your journey.
Through the magic of **mixed media art**, you’ll explore how imagery can reveal answers within, sparking creativity and fostering a deeper understanding of your unique path.

**Details:**
✨ **Location**: Wise Women Sanctuary
✨ **Schedule**: Groups meet on the 4th Monday of the month
✨ **Duration**: 3 hours
✨ **Cost**: First session free, but you will pay to reserve your space and receive a refund.

Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced artist, this workshop invites you to let your imagination soar and create meaningful art that resonates with your personal journey. Connect, create, and discover the transformative power of image and creativity at Wise Women Sanctuary.

description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

title: Yesteryear by Caro Claire Burke (option 2)
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
A modern day Christian tradwife Natalie decides with her husband to take the family to live in a farmhouse, grow their own food, raise chickens and a cow, and raise/home school their ever-increasing brood without modern influences. However -- mom is also a social media influencer who videos everything... except the nannies and farmworkers behind the scenes. She wakes up one day and she and some version of her family are in a real farmhouse (with no helpers) in 1855! How to get out of this nightmare/delusion/time travel?

"I found it to be a realy page turner--couldn't put it down. I definitely think that we should read this for our group. It's so unusual and I think it would provide fodder for very interesting discussion." - Nancy R.

"For the life of me, I can’t figure out why I kept reading this book given that most of the characters in it are deplorable. But I sure kept reading it. And then when I finished it, I wondered what kind of a person could write such a book and I was surprised when I listened to the interview that the author is actually full-fledged human being with a heart and a sense of humor. To me, that the sign of someone with tremendous craft. There are many topics in this book that I think would be a wealth for us to discuss: The double lives of social media influencers, Tradwife vs Girlboss, can we go back into the way that used to be. I suspect the reason this book is so hot because it’s so topical." - Lucinda

"It took me a bit to get into (I was just so annoyed at the beginning:) but after things began to develop, I was hooked. A lot to discuss - although it may be tough to separate out discussion on the book itself and the real-world implications!" - Debra

"[Why You Should Read ‘Yesteryear’ Now](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/10/briefing/yesteryear-caro-claire-burke.html?unlocked_article_code=1.01A.Gak9.SZGpJviEJq74&smid=url-share)" - NY Times

"‘[Yesteryear’ is this summer’s must-discuss book. We have questions.](https://www.washingtonpost.com/style/interactive/2026/06/18/yesteryear-is-this-summers-must-read-book-let-discuss/)" - Washington Post

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

title: Beginning Watercolor Class
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

For more information or to register for this class, please contact Eva at: evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com

You can also visit Eva's website at: http://evamautner.com http://evamautner.com evamautner.com

location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Thursdays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 11:30am - 1:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

title: Take the art of Still Life to new places
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Thursdays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 11:30am - 1:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.

Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner

  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work

  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

title: Sips and Stars
description:
Sips and Stars ~ an evening of fine wine and cosmic wonder.

Join us for a magical night under the stars at the Robert Ferguson Observatory! Our Sips & Stars event blends the beauty of the night sky with the elegance of Sonoma County wine. Enjoy a curated tasting experience hosted by a local winery, while taking in breathtaking views of the cosmos through our powerful telescopes.

As twilight falls, relax with a glass of wine in hand and listen to engaging astronomy talks from our knowledgeable docents. Once darkness settles, step up to the observatory’s telescopes for guided viewing of planets, star clusters, and distant galaxies.

Whether you’re a wine lover, stargazer, or simply looking for a unique evening out in Sonoma Valley, Sips & Stars promises an unforgettable experience where earthly pleasures meet celestial beauty.

Guests must be 21 or older to attend and each registration includes two drink tickets. Proceeds support the Robert Ferguson Observatory’s public education programs.

Space is limited - register at rfo.simpletix.com

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools

  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

Dates: Thursdays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 11:30am - 1:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

John of John by Douglas Stuart (option 1)
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
*Publisher's description*: A vivid, moving novel following a young man returning to his Hebridean island home, a portrait of a father's expectations and a son's desires.

Out of money and with little to show for his art school education, John-Calum Macleod takes the ferry back home to the Isle of Harris in the Outer Hebrides to find that little has changed except for him. He returns to the windswept croft and the two pillars of his childhood: his father John, a sheep farmer, tweed weaver, and lay preacher in the local Presbyterian church, and his maternal grandmother Ella, a profanity-loving Glaswegian whose steady warmth helped Cal weather the sudden departure of his mother.

Cal privately wonders if any lonely men might be found on the barren hillsides of home, while John is dismayed by his son's long hair, strange clothes, and seeming unwillingness to be Saved. But Cal isn't the only one who is keeping secrets. As lambing season turns to shearing season, the threads holding together the community together become increasingly frayed, and nothing will remain as it was before. *John of John* is a singular novel about duty, passion, and the transformative power of the truth.

*From our members*:

Mac: "a must-read for our Novel Lovers discussions. It contains beautiful, accurate descriptions of the harsh sere landscape in the Outer Hebrides where I’ve visited. It’s filled with secrets, many revealed and others not. Stuart dishes up human hope and despair in equal measure. Having dwelt on very different islands with small face-to-face communities like those on Harris and Lewis, the novel reflects life in many other places besides the far west of Scotland."

Matthew: "I did appreciate *John of John* and greatly admire Douglas Stuart's thoughtful writing. Sheep farming on a remote Scottish isle is a world so removed. It's very much an internal dialogue with the handful of characters, with a number ancillary family members and neighbors. I finished the book several weeks ago and it's stayed with me."

Ma'ayan: "I LOVED it all the way through. It broke my heart but also gave me hope. I laughed out loud at certain parts, too. The writing is so visceral. This one really stole my heart."

Joan: "So much in this book. It's about finding/denying/finding one's true self; keeping family secrets and secrets kept from family; passion and denial of passion; staying upright when family, religion, and the hardscrabble life of sheep farming on a Scottish island beat you down. Some books just get to you. This one gets to me."

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

location: Rileystreet Art Supply,1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

title: John of John by Douglas Stuart (option 2)
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
*Publisher's description*: A vivid, moving novel following a young man returning to his Hebridean island home, a portrait of a father's expectations and a son's desires.

Out of money and with little to show for his art school education, John-Calum Macleod takes the ferry back home to the Isle of Harris in the Outer Hebrides to find that little has changed except for him. He returns to the windswept croft and the two pillars of his childhood: his father John, a sheep farmer, tweed weaver, and lay preacher in the local Presbyterian church, and his maternal grandmother Ella, a profanity-loving Glaswegian whose steady warmth helped Cal weather the sudden departure of his mother.

Cal privately wonders if any lonely men might be found on the barren hillsides of home, while John is dismayed by his son's long hair, strange clothes, and seeming unwillingness to be Saved. But Cal isn't the only one who is keeping secrets. As lambing season turns to shearing season, the threads holding together the community together become increasingly frayed, and nothing will remain as it was before. *John of John* is a singular novel about duty, passion, and the transformative power of the truth.

*From our members*:

Mac: "a must-read for our Novel Lovers discussions. It contains beautiful, accurate descriptions of the harsh sere landscape in the Outer Hebrides where I’ve visited. It’s filled with secrets, many revealed and others not. Stuart dishes up human hope and despair in equal measure. Having dwelt on very different islands with small face-to-face communities like those on Harris and Lewis, the novel reflects life in many other places besides the far west of Scotland."

Matthew: "I did appreciate *John of John* and greatly admire Douglas Stuart's thoughtful writing. Sheep farming on a remote Scottish isle is a world so removed. It's very much an internal dialogue with the handful of characters, with a number ancillary family members and neighbors. I finished the book several weeks ago and it's stayed with me."

Ma'ayan: "I LOVED it all the way through. It broke my heart but also gave me hope. I laughed out loud at certain parts, too. The writing is so visceral. This one really stole my heart."

Joan: "So much in this book. It's about finding/denying/finding one's true self; keeping family secrets and secrets kept from family; passion and denial of passion; staying upright when family, religion, and the hardscrabble life of sheep farming on a Scottish island beat you down. Some books just get to you. This one gets to me."

Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

title: Deep Sky Astrophotography Processing class (class 1 of 3)
description: Have you ever admired amazing deep sky astrophotography images and wondered if you could ever create similar images?  Now you can!   With raw data provided from the telescopes at the Robert Ferguson Observatory, in this class series of three sessions you will have the opportunity to learn how to process and edit your own beautiful deep sky images. Please note, this workshop is meant as a 3-class series. It is highly recommended to purchase tickets for all three days.Please note, this is a virtual class. A Zoom link will be sent to participants prior to the class. What you will learn in this class:- The fundamentals of Deep Sky Astrophotography- An overview of image capture techniques (a dedicated, hands-on class on Deep sky image capture using your own equipment will be held later in Spring 2025)- Robert Ferguson Observatory Image capture techniques - how we captured the data that will be used in this class.- An overview of image processing techniques- An introduction to Siril, a free and open-source Astronomical Image Processing Program- A hands-on session where you will process data collected at the Robert Ferguson Observatory - A wrap-up session where you will have the opportunity to share and discuss your images with other class attendees Class Prerequisites:- A computer newer than 5-years old (the newer the better), loaded with the latest operating system- At least 8MB of RAM (more is better)- At least 50GB of free disk space (preferably a solid-state disk drive.  More storage is better)- Familiarity with creating directories, moving files between folders, setting folder and file permissions, and accessing cloud drives.Get more information and purchase tickets at rfo.simpletix.com.

description:

Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

title: Garage Jam
location: Out West Garage, 321 Second Street, Petaluma, 94952, United States
description: The Garage Jam is an open, friendly bluegrass circle that meets the first and third Monday of every month, from 6 to 8 pm. All kinds of pickers show up, from rank beginners to grizzled veterans, plus folks who just come to listen and socialize. The repertoire is straight-up traditional bluegrass, although the occasional old-time or folk-inflected choice will pop up. The format is the old-fashioned song circle, with each participant getting a turn to call a song and set its key, pace, and feel. An experienced jam leader and bass player are always present to help keep things on track. Everyone is welcome — come on down!

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Thursdays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 11:30am - 1:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!
